scope: Batch 11C: original source-linked player guidance for five champions, with explicit resource, awakening and fight-length conditions.

decisions.title: Bait the defender's Special before committing to an Invisibility loop
decisions.text: Stryfe can build Telepathic Charges through a cloak and safe Heavies, but an immediate opposing Special may remove the opening. Check enemy power and spacing before using SP1 to establish the planned attack cycle.

decisions.title: Spend charges on Concussion only when ability control matters
decisions.text: A fourth-Light ender can consume charges to apply Concussion, providing a different utility from saving them for burst. Check whether the targeted defender ability can be reduced rather than expecting node-level shutdown.

decisions.title: Reserve SP3 persistent charges for a multi-fight path
decisions.text: SP3 can help bank developed charges across eligible fights, while SP2 may provide a faster finish. Decide whether the path length supports the extra investment and inspect any Shock-related opponent protection.

decisions.title: Develop the proper receptor buff before attempting Overload
decisions.text: Super-Skrull can accumulate Fury from offense and Armor through blocking, with a receptor cycle affecting Overload. Avoid taking unnecessary block damage just to build the defensive half of the setup.

decisions.title: Choose SP1 or SP2 for the buff conversion needed
decisions.text: SP1 can convert some Fury to Armor while SP2 can move Armor toward Fury. Check the current buff mix, since a buff-removing opponent can change the next Overload payoff dramatically.

decisions.title: Use SP3 Aptitude only when the future buff cycle pays back
decisions.text: SP3 can make a longer ramp more appealing through Aptitude. Against a low-health defender or a node that strips buffs, an earlier Special may be both safer and more effective.

decisions.title: Set the opening buff pre-fight to solve the defender
decisions.text: Superior Iron Man can choose an opening buff and develop missing types from second-Medium attacks. Select the useful effect for the encounter instead of applying a fixed damage-only plan on every node.

decisions.title: Duplicate an existing buff only while it is actually present
decisions.text: Fourth-Light hits can add copies of personal buff types while SP2 supports additional copies and Armor Break. Check the active buffs and target Armor Break immunity before pursuing a large stack.

decisions.title: Save SP3 buff pauses for an encounter that lasts
decisions.text: SP3 can help maintain a developed buff package while Fury remains active, but it requires three bars. If the opponent is nearly defeated or repeatedly Nullifies, a shorter route has less exposure.

decisions.title: Read Exploit Weakness's requested attack before committing
decisions.text: Taskmaster's key damage plan asks for a particular attack type at a given moment. Check the active prompt and defender recovery instead of throwing a fixed combo that may miss the actual objective.

decisions.title: Use a safe Heavy for cooldown management
decisions.text: A Heavy can alter the Exploit Weakness cooldown, but it remains punishable if started too close to an active defender. Take an opening after a blocked Special or other genuine recovery, not while the opponent can interrupt.

decisions.title: Keep awakened Concussion progression separate from the base kit
decisions.text: The signature can reward repeated exploits with passive Concussion and improved follow-ups. An unawakened Taskmaster should not be credited with that control loop, and ability-accuracy immunity can change its value.

decisions.title: Prepare Energy before asking Heavy to apply Armor Shattered
decisions.text: Deathless Thanos develops Energy through eligible hits and can spend a developed state on a Heavy Armor Shattered opportunity. Check the counter and a safe recovery window before assuming armor control is available.

decisions.title: Use SP1 Fury or SP2 Corrosion based on opponent protection
decisions.text: SP1 can support Fury, while an Energy-funded SP2 can apply Corrosion. Against a defender protected from Corrosion, the extra resource spend may be less useful than a safer immediate Special.

decisions.title: Invest in SP3's expanded Energy ceiling only for long fights
decisions.text: SP3 can improve the Energy economy later in an encounter. If the defender's remaining health is low, a shorter SP2 cash-out may deliver more practical value than the three-bar investment.
